definition_zh: 访问；参观；拜访；探望；造访
definition_en: to go to see a person or a place, usually for a limited time and then come back
core_image: 提着礼物敲门，进屋坐一会儿，喝完茶再起身告辞
scene: 出差顺路，他拎着一盒点心敲开老师家的门，坐下喝了两杯茶才起身。On his way back from the meeting, he stopped to visit his old teacher.
sceneCN: 这里 visit 是「拜访」（第 1 个义项：到某人那里去看望）；句意为开完会往回走时，他顺道去看望了老老师。提着礼物敲门、坐下又告辞的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 探访；视察；天罚的旧说法

senses.title: To go and see a person
senses.definition: to go to a person and spend time with them, then leave again
senses.definitionCN: 到某人那里去，与他待上一段时间再离开
senses.example: On his way back from the meeting, he stopped to visit his old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 开完会往回走时，他顺道去看望了自己的老老师。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is simply the act of going to see someone; the coming and going is part of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是「前去看人」这一动作，来与去都包含在内。

senses.title: To go and see a place
senses.definition: to go to a building or town in order to look at it rather than live there
senses.definitionCN: 到某座建筑或城镇去看，而不是住在那里
senses.example: The class will visit the science museum on Friday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班星期五上午将参观科学博物馆。
senses.why: A place is visited the same way a person is: one goes there, looks, and comes away.
senses.whyCN: 地方与人一样被「拜访」：去一趟、看一看，然后离开。

senses.title: To stay somewhere for a time
senses.definition: to spend a period of time at a place as a guest rather than as a resident
senses.definitionCN: 作为客人而不是住客在某地停留一段时间
senses.example: My cousin came to visit for the whole winter holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 我表弟整个寒假都来家里作客。
senses.why: The sense stretches from a short call to a whole season, because what matters is being a guest, not the length.
senses.whyCN: 这层意思从短暂的拜访延伸到整个季节，因为关键在于是客人，而不在时间长短。

senses.title: To go to a doctor or clinic
senses.definition: to go to a doctor, dentist or clinic for help rather than having them come to you
senses.definitionCN: 自己去医生、牙医或诊所那里求助，而不是让对方上门
senses.example: You should visit a dentist if the pain lasts more than three days.
senses.exampleCN: 如果疼痛超过三天，就应该去看牙医。
senses.why: Diagnosis happens by going to the office, so the same plain verb covers a medical appointment.
senses.whyCN: 诊断发生在去诊所的过程中，于是同一个朴素动词也承担了看病的说法。

senses.title: To check a place or a site
senses.definition: to go to a place in order to inspect or check it, in official or technical use
senses.definitionCN: 为检查而前往某处，用于公务或技术语境
senses.example: Inspectors will visit the factory twice next month.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员下个月将到工厂巡查两次。
senses.why: Official inspection is a visit with a purpose, so the verb took on a checking shade without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 公务检查是一次带有目的的造访，于是这个词在不改变形态的情况下带上了核查的意味。

senses.title: To come upon someone in trouble
senses.definition: in older use, of trouble or punishment, to come upon someone
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指灾祸或惩罚降临到某人身上
senses.example: A great famine visited the region that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年大饥荒降临到这一地区。
senses.why: In older writing an affliction is said to visit people, as if it were a grim guest paying a call.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的文本里，灾祸被说成「造访」人，仿佛它是一位阴沉的不速之客。

intro.en: Visit comes from Latin visitare, to go to see, which grew from videre, to see.
intro.cn: visit 来自拉丁语 visitare（前去看望），而后者又由 videre（看）生长而来。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its frequent form visitare meant to go and see often.
items.cn: videre 意为看，其反复体 visitare 意为常常前去看。

items.en: In Roman use visitare covered visiting the sick and inspecting a province as well as private calls.
items.cn: 在罗马用法里，visitare 既包括探望病人、巡视行省，也包括私人拜访。

items.en: Old French visiter carried the verb into English, with the sense of paying a call.
items.cn: 古法语 visiter 把这个动词带入英语，含义是登门探望。

items.en: English widened it to buildings, towns and museums, all of which can be gone to and looked at.
items.cn: 英语把它扩展到建筑、城镇与博物馆，这些都可以去到并观看。

items.en: The noun visit appeared beside the verb, so English now says either pay a visit or visit.
items.cn: 名词 visit 与动词并行出现，所以现代英语既说 pay a visit，也直接说 visit。

note.en: The first group gathers the see-family, the second the words that describe different kinds of call.
note.cn: 第一组收「看」词族，第二组收描述不同性质造访的词。

entries.definition: The person who makes a visit.
An official or solemn visit, sometimes a punishing one.
To visit again, or to study something again.
Sight itself, from the same Latin verb to see.
To pay a short visit to someone.
To travel through a place looking at its sights.
To be present at an event rather than to look at a place.
To visit briefly and without an appointment.

normalIntro.en: One Latin verb to see sits under visit, visitation and vision, so the image of looking is never far away.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「看」这个动词藏在 visit、visitation 与 vision 之下，所以「看」的画面一直不远。

normal.en: Vis- means to see; visit is going there so as to see.
normal.cn: vis- 是「看」，visit 就是到那里去看。

normal.en: The visitor is the person; the visit is the call itself.
normal.cn: visitor 是人，visit 是这次造访本身。

normal.en: Pay a visit is the noun phrase; visit a friend is the verb.
normal.cn: pay a visit 用名词，visit a friend 用动词。

normal.en: Visitation is the heavy official version of the same act.
normal.cn: visitation 是同一动作里带有官方重量的版本。

normal.en: Vision shares the root and means the seeing, not the going.
normal.cn: vision 与它同根，指看的能力，而不是去的过程。

abstract.en: See a doorbell pressed once and a cup of tea poured.
abstract.cn: 想门铃被按一下，随后一杯茶被斟满。

abstract.en: Feel the short pause between greeting and leaving.
abstract.cn: 感受打招呼与告辞之间那段短短的停留。

abstract.en: Picture a guest chair that is never moved into the room.
abstract.cn: 想一把始终没被搬进屋里的客座椅子。

examples.en: We visit my grandmother every Sunday afternoon.
examples.cn: 我们每个星期天下午都去看望奶奶。

examples.en: The visitors were asked to sign the book at the door.
examples.cn: 来访者被要求在门口的本子上签名。

examples.en: A doctor visited him twice during the night.
examples.cn: 夜里医生去看过他两次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威兹特」——威兹特先生每次上门都提着礼物，一坐就是一下午。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看）→ 反复体 visitare（常常去看）→ 古法语 visiter → 英语 visit；同源词有 vision、visible。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts at going to see a person, then spreads to places, to being a guest, to seeing a doctor, to inspecting, and to trouble that comes like a visitor.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从「去看一个人」出发，再延伸到看地方、作客、看医生、巡查，以及像来客一样降临的灾祸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for a doorbell.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手按门铃。

branches.en: The person branch: a stop at an old teacher’s door.
branches.cn: 人的分支：在老师门口停一停。

branches.en: The place branch: a museum tour and a winter stay.
branches.cn: 地方分支：参观博物馆与整个寒假的作客。

branches.en: The medical branch: visiting a dentist.
branches.cn: 医疗分支：去看牙医。

branches.en: The inspection branch: inspectors arriving to check.
branches.cn: 巡查分支：检查人员上门核查。

branches.en: The old trouble branch: a famine that visits.
branches.cn: 旧的灾祸分支：饥荒的降临。

intro.en: Vis- is the Latin look; -it is the ending of the past participle, and ordinary English endings build the family.
intro.cn: vis- 是拉丁语的「看」，-it 是过去分词词尾，普通英语后缀再扩展出整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and its frequent form visitare are both well recorded, and so is the noun visitatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 及其反复体 visitare 都有文献记录，名词 visitatio 亦然。

items.example: The root is the seed of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是词族的种子。

items.example: It also gives vision and visible.
items.exampleCN: 它也给出 vision 与 visible。

items.example: The longer verb is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个较长的动词是直接来源。

items.example: It forms visiting, as in a visiting team.

definition_zh: 访问者；参观者；来客；游客
definition_en: a person who goes to see someone or to look at a place, and is not a resident there
core_image: 胸前别着访客牌，站在前台登记名字的人
scene: 前台递过来一支笔，让人把名字写进本子，再别上一枚小牌子。Every visitor must sign in before going upstairs.
sceneCN: 这里 visitor 是「来访者」（第 1 个义项：到某处去看人看地的人）；句意为每位来访者上楼前都必须登记。别着访客牌、从前台过的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A person who calls on you
senses.definition: someone who comes to your home or office for a while and then leaves
senses.definitionCN: 到你家或办公室待一会儿再离开的人
senses.example: Every visitor must sign in before going upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 每位来访者上楼前都必须登记。
senses.why: The agent ending -or turns the act of visiting into the person who does it.
senses.whyCN: 表示施动者的后缀 -or 把「访问」这一动作变成了做这件事的人。

senses.title: Someone who looks round a place
senses.definition: a person who goes to a museum, castle or town to look at it
senses.definitionCN: 到博物馆、城堡或城镇去看的人
senses.example: The museum received ten thousand visitors in its first month.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆开馆第一个月接待了一万名参观者。
senses.why: Places also have visitors, so the same word covers tourists and sightseers.
senses.whyCN: 地方也有来访者，于是这个词同样覆盖游客与观光者。

senses.title: A guest in a hospital or hotel
senses.definition: a person staying briefly in an institution, or one who comes to see a patient
senses.definitionCN: 在机构短暂停留的人，或前来探视病人的人
senses.example: Visitors to the ward are asked to keep their voices low.
senses.exampleCN: 到病房探视的人被要求放低声音。
senses.why: Hospitals publish visiting hours, and there the word means the one who comes to see a patient.
senses.whyCN: 医院公布探视时间，那里的这个词指的是来探望病人的人。

senses.title: An animal that comes to a place
senses.definition: a bird or animal that appears in a place without living there, in nature writing
senses.definitionCN: 自然写作中指不在当地居住而偶尔出现的鸟或兽
senses.example: The waxwing is a winter visitor to these gardens.
senses.exampleCN: 太平鸟是这些花园的冬季访客。
senses.why: Field guides borrowed the human word for creatures that drop in for a season.
senses.whyCN: 野外指南借用了这个指人的词，来描述某个季节才出现的生物。

senses.title: A moving thing that comes near
senses.definition: in technical use, an object that comes near another, such as a comet near the earth
senses.definitionCN: 技术用法中指针靠近另一物体的东西，如靠近地球的彗星
senses.example: Astronomers tracked a regular visitor from the outer solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家追踪了一颗来自太阳系外缘的常客。
senses.why: Astronomy keeps the metaphor of the guest who arrives, is watched, and goes away again.
senses.whyCN: 天文学保留了这位来客的比喻：来了、被打量、再离去。

intro.en: Visitor is the Latin verb visitare plus -or, the ending for the one who does the action.
intro.cn: visitor 是拉丁动词 visitare 加 -or 构成的，-or 表示做这个动作的人。

items.en: Videre meant to see; visitare meant to go to see, and visitator named the one who came.
items.cn: videre 意为看，visitare 意为前去看，visitator 则指前来看的人。

items.en: Roman visitatores inspected provinces and called on the sick, so the agent noun began in official and caring work.
items.cn: 罗马的 visitator 巡视行省、探望病人，这个施动名词一开始就用在公务与照料之中。

items.en: Old French visiteur brought both the verb and the person into English.
items.cn: 古法语 visiteur 把动词和指人的词一起带进英语。

items.en: The -or spelling settled in English while the verb kept the -it ending.
items.cn: 英语里定下 -or 的拼法，而动词仍保留 -it 词尾。

items.en: Modern life added visitor passes, visitor numbers and visiting hours, all built on this one noun.
items.cn: 现代生活又添出访客证、来访人次与探视时间，全都建立在这一个名词上。

note.en: The first group gathers the call-family, the second the words for people who come and go.
note.cn: 第一组收「造访」词族，第二组收表示来去之人的近义词。

entries.definition: The act or verb of going to see someone.
An adjective for a team or scholar that comes from elsewhere.
A formal or solemn visit, often an inspection.
The brim on a cap, which shades the eyes.
A person invited to stay or to eat with you.
A visitor who travels for pleasure.
Someone who makes a short call, at a door or by phone.
A person who lives in the place, not a visitor.

normalIntro.en: Visitor is simply the act of visiting with a person-ending on it, so the family can be read like a set of signs.
normalIntro.cn: visitor 就是「访问」这个动作加上表人的词尾，因此整个词族可以像一组标牌一样读下来。

normal.en: Add -or to visit and the action becomes a person.
normal.cn: visit 加 -or，动作就变成了人。

normal.en: The verb keeps -it; only the noun takes -or.
normal.cn: 动词保留 -it，只有名词换成 -or。

normal.en: A frequent visitor comes often; a stranger comes once.
normal.cn: 常客来得频繁，陌生人只来一次。

normal.en: Museums count visitors, hospitals list visiting hours.
normal.cn: 博物馆数参观者，医院列探视时间。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with visor, the cap brim.
normal.cn: 注意别与 visor（帽檐）混淆。

abstract.en: See a badge clipped to a coat pocket.
abstract.cn: 想一枚别在大衣口袋上的牌子。

abstract.en: Hear a pen scratching a name in a signing book.
abstract.cn: 听笔在登记本上划出一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a chair by the bed that is always folded away after the call.
abstract.cn: 想床边的椅子，探视结束后总被折起来。

examples.en: A visitor left a coat at the desk and never came back.
examples.cn: 一位来访者把外套落在前台，再也没回来取。

examples.en: The gallery is free for all visitors on Sundays.
examples.cn: 星期日所有参观者都可免费进入画廊。

examples.en: Our neighbours are frequent visitors to the seaside town.
examples.cn: 我们的邻居常去那座海滨小城。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威兹特」加个「人」——威兹特每次来都要在前台写下名字。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看）→ visitare（前去看）→ visitator（前去看的人）→ 古法语 visiteur → 英语 visitor。

sensesIntro.en: The noun names whoever goes to see: a caller at home, a tourist in a museum, someone at a bedside, a bird for a season, a comet for a night.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词指所有前去看的人：登门的来客、博物馆里的游客、病床边的人，以及来一季的鸟、来一晚的彗星。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visitor badge on a coat.
core.cn: 核心意象：大衣上的一枚访客牌。

branches.en: The caller branch: a name written in the signing book.
branches.cn: 来客分支：登记本上的一个名字。

branches.en: The sightseeing branch: ten thousand people in a month.
branches.cn: 参观分支：一个月一万名观众。

branches.en: The bedside branch: quiet voices in the ward.
branches.cn: 床边分支：病房里压低的声音。

branches.en: The bird branch: a winter guest in the garden.
branches.cn: 鸟的分支：花园里的冬季来客。

branches.en: The sky branch: a comet watched once and gone.
branches.cn: 天空分支：看一次便离去的彗星。

intro.en: The verb visit plus -or gives the person; -ation gives the formal act, and re- adds a second time.
intro.cn: 动词 visit 加 -or 得到人，加 -ation 得到正式的名词动作，re- 则添上「再一次」。

latinIntro.en: Latin visitator is recorded as the agent noun of visitare, and the pattern went through Old French visiteur.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 visitator 是 visitare 的施动名词，有文献记录，这条构词法经古法语 visiteur 传入英语。

The stem of the whole family.

definition_zh: 视觉的；视力的；可视的；视觉化的
definition_en: relating to seeing or to the pictures that the eye receives
core_image: 一张视力表挂在墙上，从上到下字母越来越小
scene: 教室里灯一关，投影在幕布上铺开一片光影，学生们抬头看画面而不看文字。The teacher used a visual aid to explain the cycle.
sceneCN: 这里 visual 是「视觉的」（第 1 个义项：与眼睛看有关）；句意为老师用直观的视觉教具讲解循环过程。灯一关、幕布亮起画面的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 视觉的；视力的；看得见的

collocations.zh: 直观教具；视觉辅助材料

senses.title: Connected with seeing
senses.definition: relating to sight or to the sense of the eye
senses.definitionCN: 与视力、与眼睛的感觉有关的
senses.example: The teacher used a visual aid to explain the cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 老师用直观的视觉教具讲解这个循环。
senses.why: The Latin root is the act of seeing, and -al simply makes an adjective of it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根就是「看」这个动作，-al 只是把它变成形容词。

senses.title: Made to be looked at
senses.definition: existing as pictures, images or graphics rather than as words or sound
senses.definitionCN: 以图片、影像或图形而非文字或声音存在的
senses.example: The report has strong visual content, with maps on every page.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告的可视内容很强，每页都有地图。
senses.why: If something is designed for the eye rather than the ear, the adjective marks it as such.
senses.whyCN: 某物若为眼睛而不是耳朵而设计，这个形容词就标出这一点。

senses.title: Of eyesight itself
senses.definition: relating to the sharpness or health of sight
senses.definitionCN: 与视力的清晰度或健康有关
senses.example: Driving tests include a check of visual sharpness.
senses.exampleCN: 驾照考试包含一项视力检查。
senses.why: Medical writing applies the adjective to the state of the eye, not to pictures.
senses.whyCN: 医学写作把这个形容词用在眼睛的状态上，而不是用在画面上。

senses.title: Something seen or shown
senses.definition: a picture, graphic or film clip used to show something, often in teaching or design
senses.definitionCN: 用来展示内容的图片、图形或影像片段，常用于教学或设计
senses.example: The slides need more visuals and fewer bullet points.
senses.exampleCN: 这些幻灯片需要更多的图像，更少的要点。
senses.why: English often turns adjectives into nouns; here the picture that supports the words takes the bare form.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词变作名词，此处用来配文字的图像直接取用了原形。

intro.en: Visual comes from Late Latin visualis, from visus, sight, which is the past participle of videre, to see.
intro.cn: visual 来自晚期拉丁语 visualis，源出 visus（视觉），而 visus 是 videre（看）的过去分词。

items.en: Videre meant to see; its past participle visus meant seen, and the noun visus meant sight.
items.cn: videre 意为看，其过去分词 visus 意为被看到的，名词 visus 意为视觉。

items.en: Visus also meant the power of sight itself, and Roman writers used it for a look or a vision.
items.cn: visus 也指看的能力，罗马作家还用它表示一瞥或幻象。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed visualis, belonging to sight, which reached English through French writings.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出 visualis（属于视觉的），经法语文献传入英语。

items.en: English took the word in the fifteenth century for what belongs to sight, especially in medicine.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入这个词，指与看有关的事物，尤用于医学。

items.en: Teaching and design then made it the everyday word for pictures as opposed to words.
items.cn: 此后教学与设计使它成为指图像、与文字相对的日常用词。

note.en: The first group gathers the sight-family, the second the words that compete with visual for pictures and looking.
note.cn: 第一组收「看」词族，第二组收与 visual 在「图像」与「看」上相争的词。

entries.definition: The adverb, in a way that concerns sight.
The power of sight, or a thing dreamed of.
To form a picture of something in the mind.
A brim or mask that shields the eyes.
Relating to light and lenses rather than the mind.
Shown as a drawing or chart.
Able to be seen at all.
Relating to hearing, not to sight.

normalIntro.en: Vis- is sight; -ual makes the adjective and -ly the adverb, so the whole set can be read from the root out.
normalIntro.cn: vis- 是视觉，-ual 构成形容词，-ly 构成副词，整组词可以从词根往外读。

normal.en: Vis- is to see, so visual is simply about seeing.
normal.cn: vis- 是「看」，visual 就是关于看的。

normal.en: Visualize puts a picture in the mind; -ize turns see into imagine.
normal.cn: visualize 把图画进脑中，-ize 把「看」变成「想象」。

normal.en: Visual aid is anything you look at while learning.
normal.cn: visual aid 是学习时用来看的任何东西。

normal.en: Pair it against auditory, which is about the ear.
normal.cn: 把它与 auditory（关于耳朵的）配成一对。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ly: visually.
normal.cn: 副词加 -ly：visually。

abstract.en: See a projector beam cutting the dark room.
abstract.cn: 想投影的光束切开漆黑的房间。

abstract.en: Feel your eyes follow a line of letters that shrinks downward.
abstract.cn: 感受眼睛跟着一行行越缩越小的字母往下走。

abstract.en: Picture a report where maps carry what the text cannot.
abstract.cn: 想一份报告，地图承担了文字讲不清的部分。

examples.en: Children learn faster when visual material is included.
examples.cn: 加入视觉材料后孩子学得更快。

examples.en: The accident left him with a visual problem in one eye.
examples.cn: 那场事故使他一只眼睛出现视力问题。

examples.en: Her memory is visual: she recalls faces but not names.
examples.cn: 她的记忆是视觉型的：记得面孔却不记得名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「微坠」——灯一暗，画面微微坠落般铺满幕布，全靠眼睛接住。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看）→ visus（视觉）→ 中世纪拉丁语 visualis → 英语 visual；同源词为 vision、visible、video。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective is about the eye in every case: the sense of sight, things made for looking at, eyesight itself, and the pictures so made.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词在每个义项里都围绕眼睛：看的能力、为看而做的东西、视力本身，以及由此得到的画面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam of light landing on a screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束光落在幕布上。

branches.en: The sight branch: an aid that helps you look and learn.
branches.cn: 视觉分支：帮助人看与学的教具。

branches.en: The picture branch: a report full of maps.
branches.cn: 图像分支：满是地图的报告。

branches.en: The eyesight branch: a test of sharpness.
branches.cn: 视力分支：清晰度的检查。

branches.en: The slideshow branch: more pictures, fewer words.
branches.cn: 幻灯分支：多图少字。

branches.en: The medical branch: a problem in one eye.
branches.cn: 医学分支：一只眼睛的毛病。

intro.en: The sight root vis- takes -ual for the adjective, -ly for the adverb and -ize for the verb.
intro.cn: 视觉词根 vis- 加 -ual 成形容词，加 -ly 成副词，加 -ize 成动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, visus and Late Latin visualis are all recorded forms of the sight family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre、visus 与晚期拉丁语 visualis 都是「看」词族的确定词形。

items.example: The root of the whole family.
It also gives video and evident.
items.exampleCN: 它也给出 video 与 evident。

items.example: It forms audiovisual with the same root.
items.exampleCN: 它与同一词根构成 audiovisual。

definition_zh: 极其重要的；至关重要的；生命的；充满活力的
definition_en: extremely important and necessary for something to continue or succeed
core_image: 病人胸口那条跳动的曲线，离开了就不会再有别的
scene: 手术室外，医生摘下口罩只说了一句，那根管子必须一直通着，否则一切都停下来。Keeping the airway open is vital in an emergency.
sceneCN: 这里 vital 是「至关重要的」（第 1 个义项：离开它就不行）；句意为在急救中保持气道通畅至关重要。胸口跳动曲线的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 至关重要的；生命的；有活力的

derivatives.zh: 维生素，原意为「生命所需的胺」

senses.title: Necessary for survival
senses.titleCN: 维持生命所必需的；致命的（旧）
senses.definition: in older use, necessary for life itself, and of an injury, threatening life
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法指生命本身所必需的，形容伤口则指危及生命
senses.example: A vital organ such as the heart cannot be replaced by any other part.
senses.exampleCN: 像心脏这样的生命器官无法由别的部位替代。
senses.why: The Latin root is life, and the earliest English sense stays closest to it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根就是「生命」，英语最早的义项离它最近。

senses.title: Extremely important
senses.titleCN: 至关重要的；必不可少的
senses.definition: so important that a thing cannot work or succeed without it
senses.definitionCN: 重要到缺了它就不能运转或成功
senses.example: Keeping the airway open is vital in an emergency.
senses.exampleCN: 在急救中保持气道通畅至关重要。
senses.why: Because what is vital keeps a body alive, the word slid from life to success and plans.
senses.whyCN: 凡关乎生命者决定身体存亡，于是这个词从「生命」滑向「成功」与「计划」。

senses.title: Full of life and energy
senses.definition: lively and energetic, used of people, cities or writing
senses.definitionCN: 形容人、城市或文字时指有生气、有劲头的
senses.example: The market is a vital place at dawn, loud with bargains.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨的市场生机勃勃，讨价还价声不断。
senses.why: The same root turns outward: a thing with much life in it is described as vital.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词根向外转：内在生命力丰沛的东西就被形容为 vital。

senses.title: The signs of life
senses.definition: in medicine, the measurable signs that a person is alive, such as pulse and breathing
senses.definitionCN: 医学中人仍然活着的可测指标，如脉搏与呼吸
senses.example: Nurses recorded his vital signs every hour through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 护士整夜每小时记录一次他的生命体征。
senses.why: Medical English fixed the plural phrase for the measures that show life is still running.
senses.whyCN: 医学英语把复数短语固定来指那些显示生命仍在运转的指标。

intro.en: Vital comes from Latin vitalis, belonging to life, from vita, life.
intro.cn: vital 来自拉丁语 vitalis（属于生命的），源出 vita（生命）。

items.en: Vita meant life, and vitalis meant belonging to life or lasting a lifetime.
items.cn: vita 意为生命，vitalis 意为属于生命的、持续一生的。

items.en: Roman writers used vitalis for air, breath and the parts of the body that keep it alive.
items.cn: 罗马作家用 vitalis 形容空气、呼吸以及维持生命的身体部位。

items.en: Old French brought the word to English as vital in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个词以 vital 的形式带进英语。

items.en: English kept the medical sense of life-giving and added the everyday sense of essential.
items.cn: 英语保留「赋予生命」的医学含义，又添上日常的「必不可少」。

items.en: Phrases such as vital role and vital signs fixed the two directions in modern use.
items.cn: vital role 与 vital signs 这类短语在现代用法中固定了这两个方向。

note.en: The first group gathers the life-family, the second the adjectives of necessity that crowd around vital.
note.cn: 第一组收「生命」词族，第二组收与 vital 挤在「必要」这一层上的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning extremely or life-dependently.
The quality of being full of life.
A substance needed in small amounts for life.
Causing death, unlike vital which sustains life.
entries.definitionCN: 致命的，与维持生命的 vital 相反

entries.definition: Needed completely; the closest synonym.
So important that the outcome turns on it.
At a point where things may change for good or ill.
Of no importance at all, and an old rival of this word.

normalIntro.en: Vita is life; every sense of vital either keeps life going or borrows its force for importance.
normalIntro.cn: vita 是生命，vital 的每个义项要么维持生命，要么借用生命之力来表示重要。

normal.en: Vita is life, so vital organs are the ones life depends on.
normal.cn: vita 是生命，所以 vital organs 是生命所依赖的器官。

normal.en: Vitality is the noun for the same life force.
normal.cn: vitality 是这股生命力对应的名词。

normal.en: Vital signs are the numbers that show life is running.
normal.cn: vital signs 是显示生命仍在运转的数字。

normal.en: Do not mix it with fatal, which ends life.
normal.cn: 不要与 fatal 混淆，后者结束生命。

normal.en: In a plan, vital means nothing works without it.
normal.cn: 用在计划里，vital 指缺了它就不成事。

abstract.en: See a line on a monitor that must not go flat.
abstract.cn: 想监护仪上一条不能拉平的线。

abstract.en: Feel a pulse under two fingers, steady and warm.
abstract.cn: 感受指下稳定而温热的脉搏。

abstract.en: Picture one stone holding up an arch, remove it and the arch falls.
abstract.cn: 想一块撑住拱门的石头，抽掉它拱门就塌。

examples.en: Sleep is vital to memory.
examples.cn: 睡眠对记忆至关重要。

examples.en: The nurse checked his vital signs before the test.
examples.cn: 检查前护士测量了他的生命体征。

examples.en: Water is vital for every living cell.
examples.cn: 水对每一个活细胞都不可或缺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外头」——外头风吹雨打，屋里的火却烧得正旺，那是活气，也是命根子。

root: 拉丁语 vita（生命）→ vitalis（属于生命的）→ 古法语 vital → 英语 vital；同源词为 vitality、vitamin。

sensesIntro.en: One root, life, opens four ways: what keeps a body alive, what a plan cannot do without, what is full of energy, and the measured signs of life.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「生命」词根向外开四路：维持身体存活的东西、计划不可或缺的东西、充满能量之物，以及可测的生命迹象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pulse line that must not go flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条不能拉平的脉搏线。

branches.en: The life branch: the heart, which nothing can replace.
branches.cn: 生命分支：无可替代的心脏。

branches.en: The plan branch: an airway that must stay open.
branches.cn: 计划分支：必须保持通畅的气道。

branches.en: The energy branch: a market loud at dawn.
branches.cn: 活力分支：清晨喧闹的市场。

branches.en: The measurement branch: pulse and breathing on a chart.
branches.cn: 测量分支：图表上的脉搏与呼吸。

branches.en: The medical branch: vital organs and vital signs read together.
branches.cn: 医学分支：生命器官与生命体征一并看。

intro.en: The life root vit- takes -al for the adjective, -ality for the abstract noun and -alize for the verb.
intro.cn: 生命词根 vit- 加 -al 成形容词，加 -ality 成抽象名词，加 -alize 成动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vita and vitalis are recorded, and so is the derived noun vitalitas in later Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vita 与 vitalis 均有文献记录，后起拉丁语中的 vitalitas 亦然。

items.example: It is the root of the family.
It also appears in curriculum vitae.
items.exampleCN: 它也出现在简历一语之中。

items.example: The adjective came to English almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词几乎原样进入英语。

definition_zh: 维生素；維他命
definition_en: one of a group of natural substances needed in very small amounts for health and growth
core_image: 早餐桌上一个小苹果和一个橙色药瓶
scene: 医生翻着化验单，说骨头长得慢不是因为吃得少，而是缺了那样一小片东西。The doctor said he needed more vitamin D from sunlight and fish.
sceneCN: 这里 vitamin 是「维生素」（第 1 个义项：少量即维持健康与生长的天然物质）；句意为医生说他需要从阳光和鱼里获取更多维生素 D。小苹果与橙色药瓶并放的早餐桌就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 同效维生素；维生素变体

senses.title: A substance the body must get in tiny amounts
senses.definition: one of a set of substances found in food, needed in small amounts, without which growth and health fail
senses.definitionCN: 食物中一组物质的任何一种，只需微量，缺了便生长受损、健康受损
senses.example: The doctor said he needed more vitamin D from sunlight and fish.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说他需要从阳光和鱼类中获取更多维生素 D。
senses.why: The word was built to name what the body must find in food, and this is that plain sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就是为指称身体必须从食物中取得的物质而造，这就是它最朴素的一层。

senses.title: A pill or tablet containing it
senses.definition: in everyday speech, a pill or tablet taken as a supplement
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中指作为补充剂服用的药片
senses.example: She keeps a bottle of vitamins beside the kettle.
senses.exampleCN: 她在水壶边放了一瓶维生素片。
senses.why: The substance is sold in bottles, so the plural came to mean the tablets themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这种物质以瓶装出售，于是复数形式就转而指药片本身。

senses.title: The letter names of the group
senses.definition: the letter and number system, from vitamin A to vitamin K, used to tell the members apart
senses.definitionCN: 用字母与数字区分成员的体系，从维生素 A 到维生素 K
senses.example: Vitamin C is easily lost when vegetables are over-boiled.
senses.exampleCN: 蔬菜煮过头时维生素 C 很容易流失。
senses.why: One family needed separate labels, and chemists simply lettered the members.
senses.whyCN: 同一个家族需要各自的名字，化学家就干脆给成员编上字母。

senses.title: A figuratively nourishing element
senses.definition: a quality or thing that a group needs for health, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体健康所需的东西，用于比喻
senses.example: For a young band, applause is like a vitamin.
senses.exampleCN: 对一支年轻乐队来说，掌声就像维生素。
senses.why: Anything that keeps a thing growing in small doses can be called a vitamin in speech.
senses.whyCN: 凡是少量就能让事物生长起来的东西，在口语里都能被叫作维生素。

intro.en: Vitamin was coined in 1912 by the biochemist Casimir Funk from vita, life, and amine, a nitrogen compound.
intro.cn: vitamin 由生物化学家冯克在 1912 年用 vita（生命）与 amine（胺）拼造而成。

items.en: Vita meant life, and the chemist took it as the first half of his new word.
items.cn: vita 意为生命，化学家取它作新词的前半部分。

items.en: Scientists first believed these substances belonged to a group called amines and joined the two ideas into vitamine.
items.cn: 科学家起初以为这些物质属于胺类，便把两个概念拼成了 vitamine。

items.en: When most proved not to be amines, the e was dropped, but the old spelling had already spread in packets and papers.
items.cn: 后来发现它们大多不是胺，词尾的 e 被删去，但旧拼法已在包装和报刊上流传。

items.en: The letters A to K were assigned to separate the members, and the names hardened around the diet.
items.cn: 人们用 A 到 K 的字母区分各个成员，这些名字便围绕饮食固定下来。

items.en: Twentieth-century advertising, from orange juice to children’s cereals, carried vitamin into ordinary homes.
items.cn: 二十世纪的广告从橙汁到儿童麦片，把 vitamin 带进寻常人家。

note.en: The first group gathers the coinage and its descendants, the second the words about food and what the body needs.
note.cn: 第一组收造词本身及其衍生物，第二组收与食物和身体所需有关的词。

entries.definition: The usual plural, seen on almost every carton.
The adjective, related to or full of vitamins.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，与维生素有关或富含维生素

entries.definition: A substance the body turns into a vitamin.
Food with vitamins added after processing.
entries.definitionCN: 加工后添加维生素的食品

entries.definition: Any nourishing substance, of which vitamins are one kind.
A simple element such as iron that the body also needs.
A product taken to add what food lacks.
The lack of such a substance, which vitamin cures.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏，维生素所治的正是这种缺失

normalIntro.en: Vitamin is a coined word, so it is remembered by its two halves and by the letters that tag the group.
normalIntro.cn: vitamin 是一个新造词，可以靠它的两个半截，以及给它们编字母的办法来记。

normal.en: Vita is life, so vitamins are the small things life needs.
normal.cn: vita 是生命，维生素就是生命需要的那点小东西。

normal.en: The old spelling vitamine kept an e from amine; the e was later dropped.
normal.cn: 旧拼法 vitamine 保留 amine 里的 e，后来删去。

normal.en: Vitamin C protects the gums; vitamin D comes from the sun.
normal.cn: 维生素 C 护牙龈，维生素 D 来自阳光。

normal.en: A deficiency means the body wanted a vitamin and did not get it.
normal.cn: deficiency 就是身体想要某种维生素却没得到。

normal.en: The bare plural vitamins often means the bottle of pills.
normal.cn: 单说 vitamins 常指那瓶药片。

abstract.en: See thin orange slices and a tiny white tablet side by side.
abstract.cn: 想薄薄的橙子片与一粒白色小药片并排。

abstract.en: Feel the sun on your arms, working unseen as a vitamin.
abstract.cn: 感受阳光落在手臂上，无声地像维生素一样起作用。

abstract.en: Picture a body with one missing piece, small as a grain.
abstract.cn: 想一具身体只缺一粒米那样大的一块。

examples.en: Oranges are a good source of vitamin C.
examples.cn: 橙子是维生素 C 的良好来源。

examples.en: Too little vitamin D weakens the bones.
examples.cn: 维生素 D 过少会使骨头变脆。

examples.en: The label lists every vitamin added to the cereal.
examples.cn: 标签列出了加进麦片的每一种维生素。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维他命」——这是旧时音译，维他之命，小小一粒，替他续命。

root: 拉丁语 vita（生命）+ amine（胺）→ 1912 年造词 vitamine → 1920 年代改拼 vitamin。

sensesIntro.en: A coined scientific word became a household one: a substance needed in trace amounts, the bottle of pills, the letter system, and any nourishment an effort needs.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个造出来的科学词变成了家常词：只需微量的物质、那瓶药片、字母编号体系，以及任何努力所需的养料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny tablet beside an orange.
core.cn: 核心意象：橙子旁的一小粒药片。

branches.en: The substance branch: something from sunlight and fish.
branches.cn: 物质分支：来自阳光与鱼的东西。

branches.en: The bottle branch: pills kept beside the kettle.
branches.cn: 药瓶分支：水壶边的药片。

branches.en: The naming branch: lost when greens boil too long.
branches.cn: 命名分支：青菜煮太久就会流失。

branches.en: The figurative branch: applause for a young band.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：年轻乐队得到的掌声。

branches.en: The diet branch: the letter on the cereal label.
branches.cn: 饮食分支：麦片标签上的字母。

intro.en: Vitamin joins the Latin life root vit- to the chemical word amine, so it is a hyphenated piece of history.
intro.cn: vitamin 把拉丁生命词根 vit- 与化学词 amine 拼合，是带着删改痕迹的历史合成词。

latinIntro.en: The first half, vit- and vita, is recorded Latin for life; the second half, amine, comes from ammonia.
latinIntro.cn: 前半 vit-、vita 是有文献的拉丁语「生命」，后半 amine 来自 ammonia（氨）。

items.example: The Latin half of the coinage.
The chemist merged it with the life root.
items.exampleCN: 化学家把它与生命词根合并。

items.example: The word lost its e when the theory changed.
items.exampleCN: 理论改变后这个词失去了 e。

items.example: It names the stuff rather than the act.
items.exampleCN: 它命名物质而不是动作。

definition_zh: 生动的；鲜明的；栩栩如生的；鲜艳的
definition_en: producing clear, strong pictures in the mind, as if seen rather than read
core_image: 一扇门推开，颜色和声音一齐涌到眼前
scene: 合上书以后，那个夏天的画面还在脑子里亮着，蝉声、树影和汗味都像刚发生。Her description of the village was so vivid that we could smell the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 vivid 是「生动的」（第 1 个义项：让人脑中浮出清晰画面与感知）；句意为她对村庄的描述太生动，我们仿佛闻到了雨味。颜色和声音一齐涌来的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 生动的；鲜艳的；栩栩如生的

senses.title: Clear enough to seem real
senses.definition: so full of detail that the mind seems to see or hear the thing itself
senses.definitionCN: 细节丰富到脑中仿佛真的看见或听见
senses.example: Her description of the village was so vivid that we could smell the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她对村庄的描述如此生动，我们仿佛闻到了雨味。
senses.why: The root means alive, and a description that makes an absent thing seem present behaves as if it were alive.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「活着」，而让不在场之物如同在场的描写，也就表现得像活着一样。

senses.title: Strong and bright in colour
senses.definition: of colours, strong, clean and immediately noticeable
senses.definitionCN: 形容颜色时指强烈、纯净、一眼就能注意到
senses.example: The doors of the old town are painted in vivid blue and green.
senses.exampleCN: 老城的门被涂成鲜艳的蓝色和绿色。
senses.why: Colour is what makes a scene jump at the eye, so the same adjective passes from detail to hue.
senses.whyCN: 颜色正是让景象直扑眼睛的东西，于是同一个形容词从细节转到色调。

senses.title: Strongly held in memory or imagination
senses.definition: of a memory, dream or image, remaining clear and forceful over time
senses.definitionCN: 形容记忆、梦或形象，久久保持清晰而强烈
senses.example: He still had a vivid picture of the first snowfall at home.
senses.exampleCN: 他对家乡第一场雪仍有一幅清晰的画面。
senses.why: What is vivid in the moment is exactly what refuses to fade, so memory and imagination are described the same way.
senses.whyCN: 当下鲜明的，正是最不肯褪色的，于是记忆与想象用了同一个形容。

senses.title: Full of life in manner
senses.definition: in older use of a person, lively and full of animation
senses.definitionCN: 旧时形容人时指活泼有生气
senses.example: Her vivid manner made the dull meeting short.
senses.exampleCN: 她活泼的举止让这场沉闷的会变短了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply alive, and the word still carries that warmth when applied to people.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层就是「有生命」，用在人身上时这层暖意仍在。

intro.en: Vivid comes from Latin vividus, lively, from vivere, to live.
intro.cn: vivid 来自拉丁语 vividus（有生气的），源出 vivere（活）。

items.en: Vivere meant to live; vividus described what was full of life or long-lived.
items.cn: vivere 意为活着，vividus 形容充满生气或长存不灭的东西。

items.en: Roman writers applied vividus to colours, to speech and to light, not only to living bodies.
items.cn: 罗马作家把 vividus 用在颜色、言语与光上，不只用于活物。

items.en: The same root gave vivere’s siblings, including vivax, tenacious of life, and vivus, alive.
items.cn: 同一词根还生出 vivax（生命力顽强）与 vivus（活的）。

items.en: English adopted vivid in the seventeenth century for bright colour and lively writing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入 vivid，用于鲜亮的颜色与活泼的文字。

items.en: Modern use keeps the double force: bright to the eye, and clear to the mind's eye.
items.cn: 现代用法保留了两重力量：眼睛看到鲜亮，心眼看到清晰。

note.en: The first group gathers the life root, the second the adjectives of bright and clear description.
note.cn: 第一组收「生命」词根，第二组收形容鲜明与清晰描写之词。

entries.definition: The adverb, in a lively and clear manner.
The quality that makes a scene seem real.
Lively in manner, said of people.
To bring to life or make lively.
So detailed that it is almost unpleasant to read.
entries.definitionCN: 描写具体到令人不适的

entries.definition: Strong in colour or light.
Without clear shape or detail.
Long and dull, sharing the root but with the life gone.
entries.definitionCN: 冗长乏味的，同词根却没了生气

normalIntro.en: The root is to live; what is vivid is alive in the eye, in the memory and in the describing words.
normalIntro.cn: 词根是「活」，凡是 vivid 的东西，都在眼睛里、记忆里和描述的文字里活着。

normal.en: Viv- is life, so a vivid scene is one that lives in the mind.
normal.cn: viv- 是生命，vivid 的场景就是活在心里。

normal.en: Vivid colours are strong; vivid writing is detailed.
normal.cn: vivid colours 指颜色强烈，vivid writing 指文字细致。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ly and keeps the same spelling.
normal.cn: 副词加 -ly，拼写不变。

normal.en: Same root as survive, which means to live through.
normal.cn: 与 survive 同根，后者意为活过来。

normal.en: Its opposite is vague, with no edges.
normal.cn: 反义是 vague，没有边角。

abstract.en: See a deep blue door on a grey street.
abstract.cn: 想灰街上的一扇深蓝的门。

abstract.en: Hear a story told so well that rain seems to fall in the room.
abstract.cn: 听一个讲得太好的故事，屋里仿佛下起雨来。

abstract.en: Feel a memory stay sharp after years.
abstract.cn: 感受一段记忆多年后仍然锐利。

examples.en: The book gives a vivid account of life at sea.
examples.cn: 这本书生动地讲述了海上生活。

examples.en: She has vivid memories of her first day at school.
examples.cn: 她对上学的第一天有清晰的记忆。

examples.en: The garden was full of vivid red flowers.
examples.cn: 花园里满是鲜艳的红花。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威威的」——颜色威威地逼上前来，画面也威威地留在脑里。

root: 拉丁语 vivere（活）→ vividus（有生气的）→ 英语 vivid；同源词有 survive、revive、vivacity。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins at being alive and ends by lending that life to descriptions, colours, memories and even manners.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「活着」起步，最后把这份生气借给了描写、颜色、记忆甚至举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opening onto colour and sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门推开，颜色与声音涌来。

branches.en: The description branch: a village one can smell.
branches.cn: 描写分支：能闻到的村庄。

branches.en: The colour branch: bright blue and green doors.
branches.cn: 颜色分支：鲜蓝与鲜绿的门。

branches.en: The memory branch: the first snowfall at home.
branches.cn: 记忆分支：家乡的第一场雪。

branches.en: The manner branch: a dull meeting made short.
branches.cn: 举止分支：沉闷的会变短了。

branches.en: The storytelling branch: words that leave a picture behind.
branches.cn: 讲叙分支：留下画面的文字。

intro.en: The life root viv- takes -id for the adjective, -ly for the adverb and -acious for the manner word.
intro.cn: 生命词根 viv- 加 -id 成形容词，加 -ly 成副词，加 -acious 成形容举止的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vivere, vividus and vivax are all recorded, and the root also survives in survive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vivere、vividus、vivax 均有文献，这个词根也存活在 survive 之中。

items.example: It is the root of the family.
It is shortened to -vive in survive.
The English word came almost unchanged.
It forms survive, to live beyond.

definition_zh: 词汇；词汇量；词语表；术语
definition_en: all the words that a person knows or that a language uses
core_image: 一叠被翻得卷角的单词卡片，从薄薄几张变成厚厚一捆
scene: 老师让学生每天在卡片上写几个新词，期末数一数，那厚厚一叠就是这一学期的收获。Reading widely is the surest way to build a larger vocabulary.
sceneCN: 这里 vocabulary 是「词汇量」（第 1 个义项：一个人掌握或一种语言使用的全部词）；句意为广泛阅读是扩大词汇量最可靠的办法。卷角卡片叠成一捆的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: All the words a person knows
senses.definition: the stock of words that one person can understand and use
senses.definitionCN: 一个人能理解与使用的全部词
senses.example: Reading widely is the surest way to build a larger vocabulary.
senses.exampleCN: 广泛阅读是扩大词汇量最可靠的办法。
senses.why: The Latin seed meant a naming or a calling, and a set of names one owns is exactly a personal word stock.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「命名」或「称呼」，一个人所拥有的名字集合正是他的词库。

senses.title: The words of a language or field
senses.titleCN: （某一语言或领域的）词汇；术语
senses.definition: the whole set of words used by a language, a subject or a group
senses.definitionCN: 一种语言、一个学科或一个群体所使用的全部词
senses.example: The vocabulary of chemistry is full of Greek compounds.
senses.exampleCN: 化学的词汇里满是希腊语的合成词。
senses.why: A trade names its own objects, so the collection of names grows into a field’s word stock.
senses.whyCN: 一个行业要为自家的事物命名，于是「名字的集合」长成了某一领域的词库。

senses.title: A list of words to be learned
senses.definition: a list of words with meanings, often arranged for study
senses.definitionCN: 带释义、常按学习次序编排的词表
senses.example: Each unit opens with a short vocabulary at the back of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 每个单元都在页后附一小段词汇表。
senses.why: Books printed such a list under the same name, and so the collection became the page you study from.
senses.whyCN: 书本也把这样的清单一并叫作这个名字，于是「汇集」变成了你研读的那一页。

senses.title: The range of expressive signs
senses.definition: the set of forms or gestures used by an art, a style or a machine, in extended use
senses.definitionCN: 在引申用法中指某种艺术、风格或机器使用的形式与语汇
senses.example: The painter kept a limited vocabulary of shapes and colours.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家只用有限的一套形状与色彩语汇。
senses.why: Once a stock of words is a set of available signs, any art with recurring forms can be said to have one.
senses.whyCN: 一旦词库被看作可用的符号集合，任何有反复形式的艺术都可以说拥有它。

intro.en: Vocabulary goes back to Latin vocare, to call, through the noun vocabulum, a name.
intro.cn: vocabulary 上溯到拉丁语 vocare（呼叫），经由名词 vocabulum（名称）。

items.en: Vocare meant to call or to name, and a vocabulum was a name, one called thing.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼叫或称呼，vocabulum 就是一个名称、一个被叫到的东西。

items.en: Medieval Latin used vocabularium for a collection of names or words, a word list.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 vocabularium 指名称或词语的汇集，即词表。

items.en: The plural vocabula covered the stock of names someone or something had.
items.cn: 复数 vocabula 指某人或某物所拥有的「名字」总和。

items.en: French vocabulary passed into English in the sixteenth century, at first as a list of hard words.
items.cn: 法语的词汇一语在十六世纪进入英语，起初指难词的清单。

items.en: The sense then grew from the list to the whole stock of words, personal or shared.
items.cn: 此后词义从「清单」扩大到全部词的总和，可属个人，也可共享。

note.en: The first group gathers the calling root, the second the words that overlap with vocabulary in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收「呼叫」词根，第二组收与 vocabulary 意义重叠的词。

entries.definition: The plural, used for several word lists.
A single word seen as a form, not a meaning.
Of the voice, from the same calling root.
A calling to a kind of work.
The full word stock of a language, a formal word.
A list of hard words with explanations.
The special vocabulary of a field.
The book that lists that word stock.

normalIntro.en: The word grew out of calling and naming, so vocabulary can be pictured as a bag of names one carries.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「呼叫」与「命名」长出来，所以 vocabulary 可以想成随身带着的一袋名字。

normal.en: Voc- means to call, so a vocabulary is the set of names you can call up.
normal.cn: voc- 意为呼叫，词汇量就是你能叫得出的名字总数。

normal.en: The plural is vocabularies, with ies for y.
normal.cn: 复数是 vocabularies，y 变 ies。

normal.en: Vocable is one word; vocabulary is the whole collection.
normal.cn: vocable 是一个词，vocabulary 是整批词。

normal.en: Vocal and vocabulary share the same calling root.
normal.cn: vocal 与 vocabulary 共享同一个呼叫词根。

normal.en: A glossary is a small vocabulary at the back of a book.
normal.cn: glossary 是书后的一小份词汇表。

abstract.en: See a bundle of cards that thickens over a term.
abstract.cn: 想一叠卡片在一个学期里越攒越厚。

abstract.en: Hear a name called out and answered at once.
abstract.cn: 听一个名字被叫到，立刻有人应。

abstract.en: Picture a toolbox where each tool has a name written on it.
abstract.cn: 想一只工具箱，每件工具上都写着名字。

examples.en: His English vocabulary grew quickly after a year abroad.
examples.cn: 在国外待了一年后，他的英语词汇量增长很快。

examples.en: Every trade has its own vocabulary.
examples.cn: 每个行业都有自己的行话。

examples.en: The teacher wrote a short vocabulary on the board.
examples.cn: 老师在黑板上写了一份简短的词汇表。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我卡比哟拉瑞」——我卡在词堆里，拉出一张又一张卡片，越拉越多。

root: 拉丁语 vocare（呼叫）→ vocabulum（名称）→ 中世纪拉丁语 vocabularium（词表）→ 法语 → 英语 vocabulary。

sensesIntro.en: A collection of names spreads from one person’s word stock to a language, to a printed list, and finally to the signs an art can use.
sensesIntro.cn: 「名字的汇集」从个人的词库，扩展到一门语言、一份印出来的词表，最后到一种艺术可用的符号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick bundle of word cards.
core.cn: 核心意象：一捆厚厚的单词卡片。

branches.en: The personal branch: a stock that grows by reading.
branches.cn: 个人分支：靠阅读增长的词库。

branches.en: The field branch: Greek compounds in chemistry.
branches.cn: 领域分支：化学里的希腊合成词。

branches.en: The list branch: a short list at the back of a page.
branches.cn: 清单分支：页后的一小段词表。

branches.en: The art branch: a painter’s few shapes and colours.
branches.cn: 艺术分支：画家有限的形状与色彩。

branches.en: The study branch: building a list into a stock.
branches.cn: 学习分支：把清单攒成词库。

intro.en: Voca- carries the calling; -bul- builds the noun of result and -ary gathers it into a collection.
intro.cn: voca- 携带呼叫之义，-bul- 构成结果名词，-ary 再把它收成一集。

latinIntro.en: Latin vocare, vocabulum and Medieval Latin vocabularium are all recorded words of this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vocare、vocabulum 与中世纪拉丁语 vocabularium 都是这一词族有文献的词形。

items.example: It is shared with vocal and voice.
It is the seed of the family.
It supplies the middle of the word.
It turns a name into a collection.

items.meaningCN: y 变 ies 的复数

items.example: It forms glossary, a small word list.

definition_zh: 嗓音；声音；意见；发言权；语态
definition_en: the sound made when a person speaks or sings, using the vocal cords
core_image: 喉咙里的声带一收一放，空气被推成能辨认出是谁的声音
scene: 电话那头只说了半句，他就听出是谁，那个声音听过太多次了。Her voice was so low on the phone that I could hardly hear her.
sceneCN: 这里 voice 是「嗓音」（第 1 个义项：说话或唱歌时嗓子发出的声音）；句意为她在电话里的声音低得几乎听不见。声带一收一放的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 嗓音；声音；意见；发言权；语态

derivatives.zh: 无声的；清音的；无发言权的

senses.title: The sound of speaking or singing
senses.definition: the sound produced in the throat when a person speaks, sings or shouts
senses.definitionCN: 人说话、唱歌或喊叫时在喉部发出的声音
senses.example: Her voice was so low on the phone that I could hardly hear her.
senses.exampleCN: 她在电话里的声音低得几乎听不见。
senses.why: The Latin word for voice named the sound itself before it named anything figurative.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语里的这个词，先指声音本身，之后才被引申他用。

senses.title: An opinion expressed
senses.definition: the opinion of a person or a group, especially as expressed aloud
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体的意见，尤指说出来的
senses.example: The voice of the staff was finally heard at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 员工的声音终于在会上被听到了。
senses.why: What is said aloud is the voice of the one saying it, so the sound stands for the view.
senses.whyCN: 说出口的话就是说话者的声音，于是声音代替了观点。

senses.title: The right to speak and be counted
senses.definition: the right or chance to express an opinion and influence a decision
senses.definitionCN: 表达意见并影响决定的权利或机会
senses.example: Students now have a voice in how the library is run.
senses.exampleCN: 学生如今在图书馆的管理上有发言权。
senses.why: If an opinion is a voice, being allowed to speak is having a voice; the right follows from the sound.
senses.whyCN: 如果意见就是声音，那么被允许开口就是有声音，权利从声音里推演出来。

senses.title: The verb, to put into words
senses.definition: to express a feeling or opinion in words
senses.definitionCN: 用言语表达感受或意见
senses.example: She voiced doubts that no one else dared to raise.
senses.exampleCN: 她说出了别人不敢提的疑问。
senses.why: English turns many nouns into verbs without change, so the thing you have can become the thing you do.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让名词原封不动地变作动词，于是你拥有的东西就变成你做的动作。

senses.title: A grammatical form
senses.definition: in grammar, the form that shows whether the subject acts or is acted upon
senses.definitionCN: 语法中表示主语是施动还是受动的形式
senses.example: The report was rewritten in the passive voice.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告改用了被动语态。
senses.why: Roman grammarians spoke of the verb’s kinds of vox, and the term was carried into English grammar.
senses.whyCN: 罗马语法学家谈论动词的种种 vox，这个术语被带入英语语法。

senses.title: In music and phonetics, the singing part
senses.definition: a line of music for singing, or the buzzing quality of certain speech sounds
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中供唱的声部，或某些语音的带声性质
senses.example: The four voices came in one after another, none too loud.
senses.exampleCN: 四个声部依次进入，都不太响。
senses.why: A part written for singers takes the name of what singers use, and phonetics borrows it for the same reason.
senses.whyCN: 写给歌者的声部取用了歌者所用之物的名字，语音学也出于同样理由借用它。

intro.en: Voice comes from Latin vox, the word for voice, through Old French voiz.
intro.cn: voice 来自拉丁语 vox（声音、话语），经古法语 voiz 传入英语。

items.en: Vox meant both the voice and what it says, and it was used for a call or an order.
items.cn: vox 既指声音，也指声音说出的话，还用作呼喊或命令。

items.en: Roman grammarians used vox to describe the forms of the verb, and the idea of grammatical voice starts here.
items.cn: 罗马语法学家用 vox 描述动词的形式，语法上的「语态」这一观念在此起步。

items.en: Old French voiz carried the word, and the spelling was fixed in English as voice.
items.cn: 古法语 voiz 把这个词带过来，英语定下 voice 的拼法。

items.en: English extended it from sound to opinion, then to the right to speak: a voice in the matter.
items.cn: 英语把它从声音扩展到意见，再扩展到发言的权利：在这件事上有声音。

items.en: Printing and later broadcasting made the voice of the people a familiar phrase.
items.cn: 印刷术与后来的广播使「人民的声音」成为常见说法。

note.en: The first group gathers the calling and voicing family, the second the words for sound and for speech rights.
note.cn: 第一组收发声与呼叫的词族，第二组收表示声音与发言权的词。

entries.definition: The plural and the third person singular.
entries.definitionCN: 复数与第三人称单数形式

entries.definition: Uttered aloud, or produced with the vocal cords buzzing.
Relating to the voice, and also outspoken.
A speech sound made with an open mouth.
Anything the ear can hear, voices included.
The colour or feeling of a voice.
A view held, whether spoken or not.
The absence of any voice.

normalIntro.en: One Latin noun for the voice supplies the sound, the opinion, the right to speak, the verb and the grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁名词同时供给了声音、意见、发言权、动词形式与语法术语。

normal.en: Voice is both what comes out and the right to let it come out.
normal.cn: voice 既是发出的声音，也是允许发出的权利。

normal.en: Raise your voice is louder; find your voice is braver.
normal.cn: raise your voice 是提高音量，find your voice 是敢于表达。

normal.en: The verb is regular: voiced, voicing.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：voiced、voicing。

normal.en: The passive voice moves the doer to the end.
normal.cn: 被动语态把施动者挪到句末。

normal.en: Vocal and vowel come from the same root.
normal.cn: vocal 与 vowel 同根。

abstract.en: See a throat move once and a room go quiet.
abstract.cn: 想喉咙动一下，房间就静下来。

abstract.en: Hear a phone voice and know the speaker at once.
abstract.cn: 听电话里的声音，立刻认出是谁。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand that is given the floor.
abstract.cn: 想一只举起的手被准许发言。

examples.en: He lowered his voice so the children would not hear.
examples.cn: 他压低声音，免得孩子听见。

examples.en: Local residents have no voice in the planning process.
examples.cn: 当地居民在规划过程中没有发言权。

examples.en: She voiced her concern about the new rules.
examples.cn: 她说出了对新规定的担忧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我嘶」——嗓子一使劲，我嘶了一声，屋里人都回头看。

root: 拉丁语 vox（声音；话语）→ 古法语 voiz → 英语 voice；同源词有 vocal、vowel、vocation。

sensesIntro.en: The word runs from the sound in the throat to an opinion, to the right to speak, to the verb of saying, to grammar and music.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从喉咙里的声音一路走到意见、发言权、动词「道出」，再到语法与音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vocal cords pushing air into a known sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：声带把空气推成熟悉的声音。

branches.en: The sound branch: a low voice on the phone.
branches.cn: 声音分支：电话里低低的嗓音。

branches.en: The opinion branch: staff heard at last.
branches.cn: 意见分支：员工终于被听到。

branches.en: The rights branch: students in library decisions.
branches.cn: 权利分支：学生在图书馆事务中的作用。

branches.en: The language branch: voiced doubts and the passive form.
branches.cn: 语言分支：道出的疑问与被动形式。

branches.en: The music branch: four parts entering one by one.
branches.cn: 音乐分支：四个声部依次进入。

intro.en: The voicing root voc- takes -al, -ize and -ation, and appears in voice, vocal and vowel.
intro.cn: 发声词根 voc- 加 -al、-ize、-ation 等后缀，出现在 voice、vocal、vowel 之中。

latinIntro.en: Latin vox with its stem voc- is recorded, and so is the adjective vocalis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vox 及其词干 voc- 有文献记录，形容词 vocalis 亦然。

items.example: It is the root of the family.
The noun itself came into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词本身进入了英语。

definition_zh: 易受攻击的；脆弱的；易受伤的；易受影响的
definition_en: easily harmed, attacked or affected, because of weakness or lack of protection
core_image: 一层铠甲上有一道没盖住的缝，箭正好能扎进去
scene: 夜里山路没有护栏，老人拄着棍慢慢走，一点风都能让人打晃。Young plants are vulnerable to frost in late spring.
sceneCN: 这里 vulnerable 是「易受伤害的」（第 1 个义项：因脆弱或缺乏保护而容易受损）；句意为幼苗容易受晚春霜冻伤害。铠甲上留着缝的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 脆弱的；易受攻击的；易受影响的

derivatives.zh: 不会受伤的；刀枪不入的

senses.title: Easy to be hurt physically
senses.definition: easily injured because of thin skin, weak health or lack of shelter
senses.definitionCN: 因皮薄、体弱或无所庇护而容易受伤
senses.example: Young plants are vulnerable to frost in late spring.
senses.exampleCN: 幼苗容易受到晚春霜冻的伤害。
senses.why: The Latin word meant wounding, so the adjective began with the body and what can cut it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词意为「致伤」，所以这个形容词从身体和能划伤身体的东西开始。

senses.title: Open to attack or criticism
senses.titleCN: 易受攻击的；易受指责的
senses.definition: weak in a way that an enemy or a critic can use
senses.definitionCN: 弱点明显，能被对手或批评者利用
senses.example: The old bridge is vulnerable to a single well-aimed charge.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧桥经不起一次准确地放置的爆破。
senses.why: A wound is not only physical, so a wall with a weak point is said to be vulnerable in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 伤口不只在身上，所以有弱点的城墙也用同一个词形容。

senses.title: Needing social protection
senses.definition: used of people or groups who need help, such as the elderly, the poor or the sick
senses.definitionCN: 形容需要帮助的人或群体，如老人、穷人、病人
senses.example: Social workers visit the most vulnerable families each week.
senses.exampleCN: 社工每周探访最脆弱的那些家庭。
senses.why: In policy writing the wounded side is a group left without cover, and the word turns into a term of care.
senses.whyCN: 在政策文本里，「会被伤到的一方」就是无处遮蔽的人群，这个词便成了照料用语。

senses.title: Easily affected by something
senses.definition: likely to be affected badly by a disease, a market or a change
senses.definitionCN: 容易因病、市场或变化而受害
senses.example: Farms here are vulnerable to a fall in the price of grain.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农场容易受粮价下跌的打击。
senses.why: Anything that can be hurt by a change of condition gets the same adjective, whether a body or a business.
senses.whyCN: 凡会因条件变化而受损的东西都得到同一个形容词，身体也罢，生意也罢。

senses.title: Defenceless in feeling
senses.titleCN: （情感上）容易受伤的；毫无防备
senses.definition: feeling exposed and easily hurt, in emotional use
senses.definitionCN: 情感层面指暴露、易被伤害
senses.example: After the move he felt vulnerable among strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 搬来以后，他在陌生人中间感到没有依靠。
senses.why: With no armour of habit or friends, the feeling is the bodily one carried inward.
senses.whyCN: 没有习惯与朋友作护甲，这种感觉就是把身体上的那层搬进了心里。

intro.en: Vulnerable comes from Latin vulnerare, to wound, from vulnus, a wound.
intro.cn: vulnerable 来自拉丁语 vulnerare（使受伤），源出 vulnus（伤口）。

items.en: Vulnus meant a wound, and vulnerare meant to inflict one.
items.cn: vulnus 意为伤口，vulnerare 意为使受伤。

items.en: Vulnerabilis described a spot that could be wounded, said of bodies and of walls.
items.cn: vulnerabilis 形容能被伤到的位置，身体与城墙都可用。

items.en: Military writers used it for the one open part of a fortification, and the military sense survives.
items.cn: 军事作家用它指防御工事里未被掩护的那一块，这一层含义延续至今。

items.en: English took the word in the seventeenth century for what can be hurt.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入这个词，指能被伤到的东西。

items.en: Modern policy language extended it to people and economies that need protection.
items.cn: 现代政策语言把它扩展到需要保护的人群与经济体。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the Latin root for a wound, the second the adjectives of weakness nearby.
note.cn: 第一组收建立在拉丁「伤口」词根上的词，第二组收近处表示脆弱的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being open to harm.
The adverb, in an exposed way.
Unable to be wounded at all.
The Latin noun for a wound.
Easily broken, of objects and health.
Left without cover or shelter.
Lacking strength, the plainest word of the set.
Unable to be beaten, the confident opposite.

normalIntro.en: The root is the wound, so everything called vulnerable has somewhere a wound can get in.
normalIntro.cn: 词根是「伤口」，凡被称为 vulnerable 的东西，都有个地方能让伤钻进去。

normal.en: Vulnus is a wound, so vulnerable means woundable.
normal.cn: vulnus 是伤口，vulnerable 就是能被伤到的。

normal.en: The noun ends in -ability: vulnerability.
normal.cn: 名词以 -ability 结尾：vulnerability。

normal.en: In- makes it safe: invulnerable.
normal.cn: 加 in- 就安全了：invulnerable。

normal.en: Vulnerable to, never vulnerable of.
normal.cn: 搭配是 vulnerable to，不是 vulnerable of。

normal.en: Old armour and young plants share the same word.
normal.cn: 旧铠甲与幼苗用的是同一个词。

abstract.en: See a gap in a metal coat where an arrow can land.
abstract.cn: 想铁衣上一道缝，箭正能落进去。

abstract.en: Hear wind against a house with no shutters.
abstract.cn: 听风吹一栋没有窗板的房子。

abstract.en: Feel a newcomer standing alone at a party door.
abstract.cn: 感受新来的人独自站在聚会门口。

examples.en: The coast is vulnerable to storms in winter.
examples.cn: 这段海岸冬季容易受风暴侵袭。

examples.en: Old people are more vulnerable to the cold.
examples.cn: 老人更容易受寒。

examples.en: The system is vulnerable because one password protects everything.
examples.cn: 一个密码保护所有东西，这个系统因此很脆弱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外了呢」——外头的护甲被卸下来了，人就没了遮挡。

root: 拉丁语 vulnus（伤口）→ vulnerare（使受伤）→ vulnerabilis（可被伤到的）→ 英语 vulnerable。

sensesIntro.en: A word about wounds moves from the body, to walls, to social groups, to markets and to feelings.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个关于伤口的词，从身体走到城墙，再到人群、市场与情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gap in the armour.
core.cn: 核心意象：铠甲上的一处缝。

branches.en: The body branch: seedlings in late frost.
branches.cn: 身体分支：晚霜里的幼苗。

branches.en: The defence branch: an old bridge, one charge.
branches.cn: 防御分支：一座旧桥与一次爆破。

branches.en: The social branch: the most vulnerable families.
branches.cn: 社会分支：最脆弱的家庭。

branches.en: The market branch: grain prices that swing.
branches.cn: 市场分支：摇摆的粮价。

branches.en: The feeling branch: a stranger among strangers.
branches.cn: 情感分支：陌生人中的陌生人。

intro.en: Vulner- is the wound; -able makes it possible, -ability makes the quality and in- removes it.
intro.cn: vulner- 是伤口，-able 表示可能，-ability 表示性质，in- 则表示取消。

latinIntro.en: Latin vulnus, vulnerare and vulnerabilis are recorded, and the wounding root appears in no other English base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vulnus、vulnerare、vulnerabilis 均有文献，这个「致伤」词根在英语里没有别的基底。

items.example: It is the only base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族唯一的基底。

items.example: It is the seed of the family.
It forms vulneraries, old wound herbs.

definition_zh: 四轮马车；货车；车皮
definition_en: a vehicle with four wheels, pulled by animals or an engine and used to carry goods
core_image: 两匹马拉着高帮的木车，轮子在土路上碾出两道深印
scene: 集市散场，帮工把菜筐一只只搬上车，车夫扯了扯缰绳，车轮吱吱地压过石板路。The wagon rolled slowly towards the river with a load of hay.
sceneCN: 这里 wagon 是「四轮马车」（第 1 个义项：由畜力或机器牵引、用于载货的四轮车）；句意为一辆装干草的马车缓缓朝河边驶去。木车在土路上留两道深印的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A four-wheeled cart for goods
senses.definition: a strong cart with four wheels, pulled by horses or oxen and used to move goods
senses.definitionCN: 四轮的结实大车，由马或牛牵引运货
senses.example: The wagon rolled slowly towards the river with a load of hay.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆装满干草的马车缓缓朝河边驶去。
senses.why: The word came from Dutch and named the plain working cart of farm and market.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自荷兰语，指农场与集市上用的一般活计车。

senses.title: A railway truck
senses.definition: in British use, an open railway truck for goods rather than passengers
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中指针运货而不载客的敞篷铁路车厢
senses.example: A long line of coal wagons stood waiting in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 调车场里停着一长列等着装煤的车皮。
senses.why: Railways simply moved the old word from the road to the rail, keeping its job of carrying goods.
senses.whyCN: 铁路只是把这个旧词从土路搬到铁轨上，保留它运货的职分。

senses.title: A covered settler vehicle
senses.definition: in American history, the covered wagon that carried families westward
senses.definitionCN: 美国历史中载着家庭向西迁徙的带篷车
senses.example: Their family crossed the plains in a single wagon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一家只靠一辆篷车横穿草原。
senses.why: The same cart, given a canvas cover, became both house and transport for settlers.
senses.whyCN: 同一辆大车加上帆布篷，就成了移民的住所兼交通工具。

senses.title: Part of a compound name
senses.definition: in compound names, a vehicle built on the same frame, as in station wagon or chuck wagon
senses.definitionCN: 复合名称中指同底盘的车型，如旅行车与流动餐车
senses.example: He parked the station wagon outside the diner.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旅行车停在餐车小馆外面。
senses.why: The carrying body of the old cart survives in names of vehicles built to hold things.
senses.whyCN: 旧大车的载货身形，存活在那些为装东西而造的车辆名称里。

senses.title: A figure for giving up
senses.definition: in the phrase fall off the wagon, to return to a bad habit such as drinking
senses.definitionCN: 在 fall off the wagon 中，指重新染上酗酒等恶习
senses.example: He stayed dry for a year and then fell off the wagon.
senses.exampleCN: 他戒了一年，后来又喝上了。
senses.why: The phrase came from temperance speech, where staying on the water wagon meant drinking no alcohol.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法出自戒酒宣传：待在运水车上，就是不喝酒。

intro.en: Wagon came into English from Dutch wagen, a word for a farm cart, in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: wagon 在十六世纪从荷兰语 wagen（农用大车）进入英语。

items.en: Wagen meant a wagon or cart, and Dutch trade and farming brought the word to England.
items.cn: wagen 意为大车，荷兰的贸易与农事把这个词带到了英格兰。

items.en: The Dutch word descends from a Germanic root for a vehicle, related to English way and to wain.
items.cn: 这个荷兰词源自日耳曼语表示车辆的词根，与英语 way、wain 有关。

items.en: English spelt it waggon for centuries, and wagon was later fixed in American use.
items.cn: 英语曾长期拼作 waggon，后来美式用法定下 wagon。

items.en: Railways gave the word a new job for goods trucks, still common in British speech.
items.cn: 铁路给它添了运货车皮的新用法，这一层在英式英语里仍然常见。

items.en: In America the covered wagon became a national image, and the station wagon followed the car.
items.cn: 在美洲，带篷车成了国民意象，汽车时代又有旅行车接续。

note.en: The first group gathers the cart family and spellings, the second the other vehicles of the road and rail.
note.cn: 第一组收大车词族与不同拼法，第二组收路上与铁道上其他的车。

entries.definition: The plural form.
The older British spelling.
The person who drives a wagon.
The road the wagon travels, from the same old root.
A cart usually has only two wheels.
A wheeled vehicle, often for passengers.
A motor goods vehicle, the modern heir of the wagon.
The British word for a large motor truck.

normalIntro.en: Wagon is a borrowed working word, so it is best held by the picture of four wheels and a load.
normalIntro.cn: wagon 是个借来的干活用的词，最好靠「四个轮子加一车货」的画面记住。

normal.en: Four wheels and a load is the whole idea of a wagon.
normal.cn: 四个轮子加一车货，就是 wagon 的全部意思。

normal.en: Wagons carry goods; carriages carry people.
normal.cn: wagon 运货，carriage 载人。

normal.en: British spelling waggon has a double g.
normal.cn: 英式拼法 waggon 是两个 g。

normal.en: A station wagon is the car version, still a carrier.
normal.cn: 旅行车是汽车版本，仍然在载东西。

normal.en: Off the wagon means drinking again, as if stepping off a cart.
normal.cn: off the wagon 指又喝上了，仿佛从车上下来。

abstract.en: See two deep ruts in a wet lane.
abstract.cn: 想湿泥路上两道深辙。

abstract.en: Hear a wooden wheel creak over stone.
abstract.cn: 听木轮在石板上吱吱作响。

abstract.en: Feel a heavy load settle and the cart push forward.
abstract.cn: 感受重货落稳，车往前一推。

examples.en: They loaded the wagon with apples before dawn.
examples.cn: 天亮前他们把苹果装上了马车。

examples.en: A line of wagons waited outside the mill.
examples.cn: 一列车等在磨坊外。

examples.en: The children rode in the back of the wagon.
examples.cn: 孩子们坐在马车后斗里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挖根」——车轮太重，把路上的土挖出了两道深根似的辙。

root: 荷兰语 wagen（大车）→ 英语 wagon；更早源自日耳曼语表示车辆的词根，与 way、wain 同源。

sensesIntro.en: One working cart spreads into the railway truck, the settler’s covered wagon, the modern estate car and one old drinker’s idiom.
sensesIntro.cn: 一辆干活的大车，扩展成铁路车皮、移民的篷车、现代的旅行车，以及一句老酒鬼的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four wooden wheels under a load.
core.cn: 核心意象：一车货下的四个木轮。

branches.en: The farm branch: hay going down to the river.
branches.cn: 农事分支：干草车往河边走。

branches.en: The railway branch: coal trucks in the yard.
branches.cn: 铁路分支：调车场里的煤车。

branches.en: The settler branch: one wagon across the plains.
branches.cn: 移民分支：一辆车横穿草原。

branches.en: The car branch: the estate car outside a diner.
branches.cn: 汽车分支：小馆外的旅行车。

branches.en: The idiom branch: sober for a year, then not.
branches.cn: 习语分支：戒了一年，又喝了。

intro.en: Wagon is a whole borrowed word; its parts are old Germanic, and the family grows with -er and the spelling waggon.
intro.cn: wagon 是整词借入，其内部构件属古日耳曼语，词族靠 -er 与拼法 waggon 扩展。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the word is Germanic and came through Dutch, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，属日耳曼语并经由荷兰语传入，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: The root is shared with way.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 way 共用。

items.example: The direct source of the English word.
The Dutch ending stayed in English.
items.exampleCN: 荷兰语词尾留在了英语里。

items.example: Same old root, a different branch.

definition_zh: （餐馆的）服务员；侍者；男招待
definition_en: a man whose job is to bring food and drink to people at tables in a restaurant
core_image: 一只手托着盘子，从几张桌子之间侧身穿过
scene: 晚饭时分，他一手稳着两只盘子，一手拎着水壶，从挤满人的过道里穿过。The waiter brought the bill without being asked.
sceneCN: 这里 waiter 是「服务员」（第 1 个义项：餐厅里给人上菜上酒的人）；句意为服务员没等招呼就把账单送来了。托盘侧身穿桌的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

collocations.phrase: ask the waiter for the bill

senses.title: A man serving at tables
senses.definition: a man employed in a restaurant to bring food and drink and to look after the tables
senses.definitionCN: 餐厅雇用的男子，负责端送饮食并照看餐桌
senses.example: The waiter brought the bill without being asked.
senses.exampleCN: 服务员没等招呼就把账单送来了。
senses.why: The agent ending -er names the one who waits, and serving at table is the oldest surviving job for this word.
senses.whyCN: 表人的 -er 后缀指「侍候的人」，而递菜上桌是这个词留到今天最古老的一份活计。

senses.title: A person who brings something
senses.definition: in older use, anyone who brings something to another person
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法指任何把东西端送给别人的人
senses.example: The waiter of good news was paid a month in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 带来好消息的那个人被预付了一个月的钱。
senses.why: Before the restaurant sense narrowed, a waiter was simply who brought something, and a few old phrases keep it.
senses.whyCN: 在餐饮义收窄之前，waiter 就是端送东西的人，少数旧语中仍见这一层。

senses.title: In compound titles
senses.definition: in job titles such as head waiter, the person in charge of other waiters
senses.definitionCN: 在 head waiter 等职务名中，指管其他服务员的领班
senses.example: The head waiter seated the guests by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 领班把客人安排在窗边。
senses.why: Compound titles simply add a rank word in front, and head names the one at the front of the line.
senses.whyCN: 复合头衔只是在前头加一个表示等级的词，head 就指站在队列最前的那一个。

senses.title: A serving tray stand
senses.definition: in old British use, a small stand or tray used for serving
senses.definitionCN: 旧英式用法中指上菜用的小架子或托盘
senses.example: The waiter stood beside the sideboard with the teapot.
senses.exampleCN: 托盘架立在餐边柜旁，上面放着茶壶。
senses.why: An object that serves the table was named after the one who serves, and the use has almost died out.
senses.whyCN: 为餐桌服务的器物以服务的人命名，这个用法如今几乎消失。

intro.en: Waiter is the French verb waitier and its English form wait plus -er, the person who waits on others.
intro.cn: waiter 是法语 waitier 的英语形 wait 加 -er，指侍候别人的人。

items.en: The root is Germanic and meant to watch or guard, and that sense stood inside the French verb.
items.cn: 这个词根源出日耳曼语，意为看守或警戒，这层意思藏进了法语动词。

items.en: Old French waitier meant to watch, and then to stay expecting, which English took as wait.
items.cn: 古法语 waitier 意为看守，继而指守候，英语以 wait 承之。

items.en: To wait on someone meant to attend to them at table, so a waiter was the one who did it.
items.cn: wait on 某人意为在桌边照应，于是 waiter 就是做这件事的人。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word narrowed to the restaurant trade.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，这个词收窄到餐饮行业。

items.en: The feminine waitress came later as a separate form; many places now use waiter for both.
items.cn: 阴性形式 waitress 后起而独立，如今不少地方用 waiter 兼指男女。

note.en: The first group gathers the waiting family, the second the staff who work the room.
note.cn: 第一组收 waiting 词族，第二组收在餐厅里干活的人。

entries.definition: To stay until something happens, or to attend on someone.
The older feminine form of the same job.
entries.definitionCN: 女服务员，旧的分性形式

entries.definition: The act of waiting, or serving at table.
The plural, with -s added to the whole word.
A neutral word for the same job, now common in America.
One who clears tables, below the waiter in rank.
entries.definitionCN: 清桌杂工，地位低于服务员

entries.definition: One who serves drinks at a counter.
The person who is served.

normalIntro.en: Wait means to attend on, and -er makes the person, so a waiter is simply the one who waits on the table.
normalIntro.cn: wait 有「侍候」之义，-er 表人，所以 waiter 就是在桌边侍候的人。

normal.en: Wait means attend on; add -er and you have the one who attends.
normal.cn: wait 意为侍候，加 -er 就是侍候的人。

normal.en: The verb is two syllables in speech: wait-er.
normal.cn: 口语里是两个音节：wait-er。

normal.en: Waitress is the older feminine form; server is the neutral one.
normal.cn: waitress 是较旧的分性形式，server 是中性的。

normal.en: To wait on a table is what the job means, not to stand and wait.
normal.cn: wait on a table 指在桌边照应，不是站着干等。

normal.en: The head waiter leads the others.
normal.cn: head waiter 带领其余的人。

abstract.en: See a tray balanced on one hand.
abstract.cn: 想托盘稳稳架在一只手上。

abstract.en: Hear a pen tap a pad as an order is taken.
abstract.cn: 听点单时笔在小本上点点划划。

abstract.en: Picture a coat putting a glass down without a sound.
abstract.cn: 想一杯水被放下而几乎没有声音。

examples.en: The waiter wrote down our order on a small pad.
examples.cn: 服务员在小本上记下我们要点的东西。

examples.en: Ask the waiter for another glass, please.
examples.cn: 请向服务员再要一个杯子。

examples.en: He worked as a waiter in the holidays.
examples.cn: 他假期里当过服务员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂它」——你喂它上菜，它喂你吃饭，托盘一端就是它。

root: 日耳曼语「看守」词根 → 古法语 waitier（守候）→ 英语 wait → wait + -er → waiter。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins at watching and attending, so a waiter is one who attends on people, at tables above all.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「看守、守候」开始，所以 waiter 是照应别人的人，最主要的场合就是餐桌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tray carried through a noisy room.
core.cn: 核心意象：托盘穿过喧闹的房间。

branches.en: The table branch: a bill set down unasked.
branches.cn: 餐桌分支：不待开口送上账单。

branches.en: The bringer branch: one who brings good news.
branches.cn: 端送分支：带来好消息的人。

branches.en: The rank branch: a head waiter by the window.
branches.cn: 职级分支：窗边的领班。

branches.en: The object branch: an old stand with a teapot.
branches.cn: 器物分支：放着茶壶的旧托盘架。

branches.en: The service branch: somebody who attends on somebody.
branches.cn: 服务分支：某人在照应某人。

intro.en: The verb wait plus -er makes the person; -ress made the old feminine form.
intro.cn: 动词 wait 加 -er 得到表人名词，-ress 曾造出阴性形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the word came through French from a Germanic root, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，由日耳曼语词根经法语传入，因此拉丁条目为空。

definition_zh: 走；步行；散步；（名词）步行；步道
definition_en: to move forward on your feet at a normal speed, with one foot always on the ground
core_image: 两只脚交替落地，一脚抬起时另一脚仍踏在地上
scene: 雨停了，他不急，沿着湿石子路一步步往回走，鞋底在水里留下印子。We walked to the station instead of taking the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 walk 是「步行」（第 1 个义项：用脚按正常速度前进，总有一只脚在地上）；句意为我们是走到车站去的，没坐公交。两脚交替落地的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: To go on foot at an ordinary pace
senses.definition: to move along on your feet at a usual speed, always with one foot down
senses.definitionCN: 用脚以平常速度前进，始终有一只脚落地
senses.example: We walked to the station instead of taking the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们是走到车站去的，没坐公交。
senses.why: This is the plain bodily sense of the oldest verb, and everything else is built on it.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个古老动词最朴素的身体义，其余各层都建立在其上。

senses.title: To take an animal out
senses.definition: to take a dog or horse for exercise on foot
senses.definitionCN: 带着狗或马步行活动
senses.example: He walks the dog before breakfast every day.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早饭前遛狗。
senses.why: English lets the verb take the animal as its object, so walking can be done to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许这个动词带动物作宾语，于是「走」也可以对别人去做。

senses.title: To go to a place as a walk
senses.definition: to cover a distance or reach a place by walking rather than riding
senses.definitionCN: 以步行的方式走过一段距离或到达某处
senses.example: She walks five miles to work every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上走五英里路去上班。
senses.why: A distance is what walking produces, so the verb can take it as an object of measure.
senses.whyCN: 距离是行走的产物，所以这个动词可以用它作计量的宾语。

senses.title: Of a thing, to go over or across
senses.definition: of an object or a look, to move over a surface or among people
senses.definitionCN: 指物体或目光在表面或人群中移动
senses.example: His eyes walked slowly over the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 他的目光缓缓扫过那封信。
senses.why: Anything that moves steadily over a surface can borrow the verb of feet.
senses.whyCN: 凡在表面上稳稳移动的东西，都能借用脚的动词。

senses.title: A journey on foot
senses.definition: an outing or a distance covered on foot
senses.definitionCN: 一段步行的外出或距离
senses.example: We went for a long walk in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到山里长距离散步。
senses.why: The verb became a noun for the outing itself, as with most simple motion verbs.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词变作了指这次外出的名词，多数简单动作动词都如此。

senses.title: A path or a way
senses.definition: a route made for walking, often marked, or the way someone walks in sport
senses.definitionCN: 供人行走的、常带标记的路线，也指运动中某人的走法
senses.example: There is a raised walk along the south wall.
senses.exampleCN: 南墙边有一条垫高的步道。
senses.why: A place made for walking is named after the act, and sport names a person’s manner by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 专为行走而设的地方以这个动作命名，运动里也用同一个词指某人的走法。

intro.en: Walk comes from Old English wealcan, to roll or toss, and its walking sense grew out of that rolling motion.
intro.cn: walk 来自古英语 wealcan（滚动、翻动），步行的义正是从这种滚动之感生长出来的。

items.en: Wealcan meant to roll or toss about, and was used of turning things over.
items.cn: wealcan 意为滚动、翻动，用于把东西翻过来。

items.en: A second form, weak in grammar, took the walking sense and became the everyday verb.
items.cn: 另有一形为弱变化，承下步行的义，成为日常用的动词。

items.en: By Middle English walk had spread from walking on foot to walking a horse or a dog.
items.cn: 到中古英语，walk 已从步行扩展到牵着马或狗走动。

items.en: The noun walk then named both the outing and the route taken.
items.cn: 名词 walk 随后既指这次外出，也指所走的路线。

items.en: Walking became a health word in the twentieth century, with step counts and walking clubs.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，步行成了健康话题，出现了记步数与步行俱乐部。

note.en: The first group gathers the walking family, the second the verbs of moving on foot at different speeds.
note.cn: 第一组收步行词族，第二组收不同速度的走动动词。

entries.definition: Third person singular, and also the plural noun.
entries.definitionCN: 第三人称单数与复数名词

entries.definition: A person who walks, or a frame for support.
The activity of going on foot.
A path fitted for walking.
To walk slowly for pleasure.
To walk in step with others, as soldiers do.
To walk a long way in the country.
To move with a moment when both feet leave the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 跑，与步行交替落地的区别在此

normalIntro.en: Walk comes from an old verb to roll; think of the body rolling over one foot, then the other.
normalIntro.cn: walk 出自一个意为「滚动」的古动词；想身体轮流压过一只脚再一只脚地滚过去。

normal.en: Walk, not run: one foot is always on the ground.
normal.cn: walk 与 run 的区别：总有一只脚在地上。

normal.en: Take a walk is the idiom for a pleasure outing.
normal.cn: take a walk 是散步的固定说法。

normal.en: You walk the dog, so an animal can be the object.
normal.cn: walk the dog，所以动物可作宾语。

normal.en: A walk is both the outing and the route.
normal.cn: a walk 既是这次散步，也是那条路。

normal.en: Walk and talk share the idea of going forward; the k keeps walk solid.
normal.cn: walk 与 talk 都指往前，结尾的 k 让 walk 咬得住。

abstract.en: See two shoes print a wet path.
abstract.cn: 想两只鞋在湿路上留出一串印子。

abstract.en: Feel the ground push back under each step.
abstract.cn: 感受每一步地面推回来。

abstract.en: Picture a raised path along an old wall.
abstract.cn: 想一条沿旧墙垫高的步道。

examples.en: I walked home in the rain.
examples.cn: 我冒雨走回了家。

examples.en: Let us take a short walk before dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭前我们散会儿步吧。

examples.en: She walks her dog along the river every morning.
examples.cn: 她每天早晨沿河遛狗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「走」——英文里最像脚步声的一个词，走一步，走一步。

root: 古英语 wealcan（滚动、翻动）→ 分化出表示步行的弱变化动词 → 现代英语 walk。

sensesIntro.en: Out of an old verb of rolling come the feet, the dog, the miles covered, the eye over a page, the outing and the path.
sensesIntro.cn: 从古老的「滚动」动词里长出脚、狗、走过的里程、扫过纸页的目光、一次外出与一条路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet taking turns on the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：两脚轮流落在地上的。

branches.en: The feet branch: to the station instead of the bus.
branches.cn: 脚步分支：走到车站而不坐车。

branches.en: The dog branch: before breakfast, every day.
branches.cn: 遛狗分支：每天早饭前。

branches.en: The mileage branch: five miles to work.
branches.cn: 里程分支：走五英里去上班。

branches.en: The look and the outing branch: eyes down a letter, a walk in the hills.
branches.cn: 目光与外出分支：扫过信纸的目光，山里的一次散步。

branches.en: The path branch: a raised walk by a wall.
branches.cn: 路线分支：墙边一条垫高的步道。

intro.en: Walk is a whole old verb; the family comes from English endings such as -er, -ing and the compound walkway.
intro.cn: walk 是完整的古动词，词族由 -er、-ing 以及 walkway 这样的复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, with no Latin source, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本族英语词，没有拉丁语来源，因此拉丁条目为空。

definition_zh: 墙；墙壁；围墙；屏障
definition_en: a solid upright structure of brick or stone, built to enclose or divide an area
core_image: 一层层砖叠起来，从地面一直到齐眉高
scene: 院子里只有一堵矮砖墙，靠墙放着几把椅子，下午日光都落在墙面上。A low stone wall runs along the edge of the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 wall 是「墙」（第 1 个义项：为围住或分隔地方而砌的直立结构）；句意为一道矮石墙沿花园边缘延伸。砖一层层叠起的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The outside wall of a building
senses.definition: one of the upright sides of a building that holds up the roof and keeps out weather
senses.definitionCN: 建筑直立的一侧，撑住屋顶并挡住风雨
senses.example: A low stone wall runs along the edge of the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 一道矮石墙沿着花园边缘延伸。
senses.why: The Latin word meant a rampart, and the first English sense is a defence you can touch.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词意为壁垒，英语最早的一层就是一道能摸得到的防御。

senses.title: A wall inside a room
senses.definition: the inner surface of a room, where things are hung or painted
senses.definitionCN: 房间的内表面，可以挂东西或刷颜色
senses.example: The painting hangs on the wall above the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅画挂在书桌上方的墙上。
senses.why: From the outside of a house the word steps inside, where the same surface is seen from within.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从房屋的外侧走进屋内，同一面被从里侧看见。

senses.title: A fence of brick or stone
senses.definition: a structure built to enclose a garden or field rather than to hold a roof
senses.definitionCN: 用来围住园子或田地、而不是用来撑屋顶的结构
senses.example: They built a wall around the orchard to keep out deer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们围着果园砌了墙，挡住鹿群。
senses.why: An enclosed field needs a barrier that lasts for years, and masonry does the job.
senses.whyCN: 围起来的田地需要一道能撑很多年的阻隔，砖石正好胜任。

senses.title: A barrier of any kind
senses.definition: in figurative use, anything that blocks movement, feeling or understanding
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法中指阻碍行动、感情或理解的东西
senses.example: A wall of silence met every question.
senses.exampleCN: 每个问题遇到的都是一堵沉默的墙。
senses.why: If a wall stops a person, then anything that stops the mind may be called a wall too.
senses.whyCN: 墙能挡住人，那么凡能挡住心思的东西也可以叫作墙。

senses.title: A mass rising like a wall
senses.definition: a mass of water, fire or stone that rises steeply and blocks the way
senses.definitionCN: 像墙一样陡立、挡住去路的水、火或石
senses.example: The wave came in as a white wall of water.
senses.exampleCN: 那道浪像一堵白色的水墙扑过来。
senses.why: A steep upright face looks like masonry, so water and fire take the same name.
senses.whyCN: 陡立的一面看起来就像石砌的墙，于是水与火也用同一个名。

senses.title: The verb, to enclose
senses.definition: to surround a place with a wall, or to stop it up
senses.definitionCN: 用墙围住某处，或把某处堵上
senses.example: The old town is walled and gated on every side.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城四周都有墙与城门。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb of building, one of the commonest shifts in English.
senses.whyCN: 名词变作建筑动词，这是英语里最常见的转换之一。

intro.en: Wall comes from Latin vallum, a rampart of earth or stakes, through Old English weall.
intro.cn: wall 来自拉丁语 vallum（土筑壁垒），经古英语 weall 传入英语。

items.en: Vallum meant a rampart or palisade, the earth and stakes of a Roman camp.
